name: Zoth ZeUSD
oneLiner: ZeUSD is Zoth's deprecated V1 RWA-collateralized debt-position dollar token; its tracked router is paused and V2 is separate.
collateral: U.S. Treasury bills, ETFs, money market funds, and reverse repos (off-chain), and tokenized on-chain RWAs (e.g., Hashnote USYC, Matrixdock STBT, OpenEden TBILL); held in smart contract escrow vaults or traditional/omnibus escrow accounts
pegMechanism: Zoth documents ZeUSD as an RWA-collateralized debt position: issuers deposit eligible RWAs, mint under Safe LTV constraints, burn ZeUSD to reclaim collateral, and collateral can be liquidated or reinvested according to its LTV. The tracked deprecated V1 router records deposit metadata and is paused, so current enforcement and operability must not be inferred from the documentation alone.

notices.title: March 2025 exploit history
notices.message: Zoth suffered March 2025 exploits affecting ZeUSD platform risk, including a collateral-accounting bug and a later admin-key compromise. Review current redemption and reserve evidence before assuming normal peg liquidity. https://www.halborn.com/blog/post/explained-the-zoth-hack-march-2025

notices.title: Severe residual depeg
notices.message: By late June 2026, ZeUSD market pricing and public liquidity remained far below the $1 peg after the 2025 exploit history, with supply reduced to a small residual base. Treat ZeUSD as a high-risk legacy/depeg case unless current issuer redemption and reserve evidence is independently revalidated.

mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Zoth's official ZeUSD mechanics describes eligible RWA deposits as opening collateralized debt positions subject to Safe LTV ratios, with repayment/redemption and liquidation of the position. The tracked deprecated V1 deployment pairs its Router with a ZeDP NFT; its verified Router and CollateralVault implementations mint a per-position ZeUSD amount from collateral price and configured LTV, then require that recorded amount to be burned before withdrawal. Within Pharos's closed taxonomy, cdp is the closest collateralized-position class rather than a fiat issuer-reserve, Treasury-fund, or RWA-credit-fund mechanism. This classification does not assert decentralized governance or a currently executable liquidation route; the existing legacy/depeg and redemption-control caveats remain separately material.
